title: Reasons for Sharp Decline in Dengue Cases Reported in 2025
what_it_is: Reasons for Sharp Decline in Dengue Cases Reported in 2025

sections.label: Dengue decrease and Wolbachia expansion
sections.summary: Dengue fell due to no major local outbreaks, global decline in 2025 and stakeholder efforts, with Project Wolbachia expanding to 800,000 households by end-2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: An absence of major local outbreaks locally, the global decline in dengue cases in 2025 and concerted efforts by all stakeholders and residents in Singapore to control the mosquito population, collectively contributed to the decrease.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency's (NEA's) holistic dengue control strategy, which combines Project Wolbachia, vector control operations and actions by all to keep premises free of mosquito breeding, continue to help keep dengue incidence low.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: By March 2026, Project Wolbachia will be expanded to cover 740,000 households, up from 580,000 households in April 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: By end-2026, Project Wolbachia will be released to cover 800,000 households or 50% of all households in Singapore, covering the majority of areas at risk of large dengue outbreaks.

sections.label: Project Wolbachia performance
sections.summary: Project Wolbachia is part of NEA's strategy and reduced dengue transmission risk by more than 70% in release areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: As I shared, Project Wolbachia is part of NEA's comprehensive strategy to suppress mosquito population and manage dengue risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: It has demonstrated good performance, as the Member has highlighted, reducing the risks of dengue transmission by more than 70% in release areas.

sections.label: Global and local dengue decline
sections.summary: Global dengue cases fell from 14.4 million to five million in 2025, and locally there is an absence of clusters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: Globally, in 2025, we also saw a decrease in dengue cases from 14.4 million for the year before, to five million; and locally, as I said just now, there is absence of local clusters as well.

sections.label: Expansion pace and site selection
sections.summary: Finite resources and mosquito suppression speed influence expansion pace, and new sites will be announced later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: Resources are finite and so the pace of expansion is also influenced by how quickly mosquito populations can be suppressed, which depends on the local mosquito situation and prevalence of mosquito breeding habitats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: And then, on a forward-looking basis, figuring out which sites, then, have a higher incidence and also, the local population of these mosquitoes, for us to decide when the sites will be expanded into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: So, in due course, we will be announcing where the new sites will be as we lead up to further expansions towards the end of the year.
